clue.text: Lead on men at dice, losing heads

indicators.note: each of the three words drops its first letter, its head, so the opening letters go

explanation.surface: Gamblers at the dice table are being led astray and losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heads' removes the first letters M, A and D from MEN, AT and DICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt or lure someone along is to entice them.

clue.text: . Cutter ending up in an arm of the lake

definitions.text: Cutter ending up in an arm of the lake

parts.words: Cutter ending up in an arm of the lake
parts.note: in Arthurian legend the dying king's sword is thrown back and caught by an arm rising from the water

explanation.surface: A blade finishes its days grasped by a hand from the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's legendary sword was returned to the Lady of the Lake.

clue.text: One prepared to take orders will -find this less of a shock

definitions.text: One prepared to take orders will -find this less of a shock

parts.words: One prepared to take orders will -find this less of a shock
parts.note: a novice monk entering holy orders has the crown shaved, leaving less of a shock of hair

explanation.surface: A recruit ready to obey commands will not be so surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaved crown of a monk's head marks entry into religious orders.

clue.text: The end is nigh

definitions.meaning: the conclusion or finish of something

explanation.definitionFit: It means both a conclusion and nearby.

clue.text: Sergeant major considering having no starter, messing

indicators.note: the synonym loses its opening letter, its starter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: considering a case means judging it

explanation.surface: A sergeant major mulls over a mess with nothing to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no starter' takes the J off JUDGING, leaving UDGING.
explanation.definitionFit: Smearing or blurring something is making a mess of it.

clue.text: As revolutionary moderniser, have this architect

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns things, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: This designer was a radical modern architect.
explanation.walkthrough: The German-American architect behind Modernism's 'less is more' fits the surface's revolutionary moderniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe was a leading Modernist building designer.

clue.text: Old soldier's run away — one not to be trusted

parts.note: to desert is to run away from duty
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A veteran has fled the army and turned traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran of Britain's 7th Armoured Division is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Suggested one politician's on song

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: Someone hinted that a politician is singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinting at something without stating it outright is to have indicated it indirectly.

clue.text: Doll's surprised expression

definitions.meaning: short for golliwog, an old rag-doll toy

explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old toy figure and is an exclamation of mild astonishment.

clue.text: High in Oxford, attractively sleepy part of town for Arnold

definitions.text: High in Oxford, attractively sleepy part of town for Arnold

parts.words: High in Oxford, attractively sleepy part of town for Arnold
parts.note: the poet Matthew Arnold described the city's lofty church towers as drowsing, a famous phrase

explanation.surface: Oxford's High Street area seemed pleasantly drowsy to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The High is Oxford's main street, which makes 'High' look like a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold's poem Thyrsis coined this phrase for Oxford's skyline of towers.

clue.text: Gathering a number 'on oath have admitted nothing

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

indicators.note: the swearing takes in, admits, the zero placed inside it

parts.note: an oath can be a swear word, a curse
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A crowd of people swear an oath that they have admitted nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a crowd or assembly of people coming together.

clue.text: One providing tight protection round' petal at first?

definitions.text: One providing tight protection round' petal at first?

parts.words: One providing tight protection round' petal at first?
parts.note: a leaf of the outer calyx wraps closely around the bud before the flower opens

explanation.surface: Something wraps protectively around a flower part in its early stage.
explanation.definitionFit: This leaf-like part of a flower encloses the petals in the bud.

clue.text: Unpleasant person left by the river

parts.note: the Ouse is a well-known English river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A nasty character has been abandoned beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex).
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a parasite or vermin, a contemptible person, is a common insult.

clue.text: Notice saint, in 'truth, suffering

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice

indicators.note: the saint's letter sits inside the word for truth

parts.note: verity means truth

explanation.surface: A notice says a saint is truly suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship or misfortune is what suffering amounts to here.

clue.text: Toast, perhaps, this traditional father's achievement?

definitions.text: Toast, perhaps, this traditional father's achievement?

parts.words: Toast, perhaps, this traditional father's achievement?
parts.note: toast is made from a loaf, so the one who gets it is a winner of loaves; and the traditional father earns the family's keep

explanation.surface: Dad is being toasted for his old-fashioned achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: The family member who earns the household's income is its main wage earner.

clue.text: Dirty room free in student accommodation

indicators.note: the letters are set free, released to form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A messy room in a student hall is available.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of residence or shared sleeping quarters houses students.

clue.text: Pair tick off Italian cathedral

indicators.note: the short moment is taken off the Italian building

parts.note: duomo is the Italian word for a cathedral
a mo is a moment, as is a tick

explanation.surface: Two visitors are scolded at an Italian cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick off' looks like 'reprimand', but 'tick' is a moment and 'off' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people performing together make a twosome.

clue.text: Public's admitted in the vicinity from day to day

indicators.note: the open word lets in the nearness word, holding it inside

parts.note: overt means open, public
nigh means near, in the vicinity

explanation.surface: People nearby have been let in, day after day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting through the night, from one day into the next.

clue.text: Computer memory crash

definitions.meaning: random access memory, the working memory of a computer
to crash into something, to butt or drive into it violently

explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names working computer storage; to smash into is the verb sense.

clue.text: Robberies in the East End? Poor me!

indicators.note: the Cockney accent of London's East End drops the final g of -ing

parts.note: muggings are street robberies

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans being robbed in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Cockney speech says 'muggin's'; London's East End is its traditional working-class district.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-mocking word for oneself as a fool or dupe.

clue.text: The Spanish bash German about how unfortunate

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces is turned round, read from the end

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
to batter is to bash

explanation.surface: A Spanish attack on a German is a sorry affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole of ELBATTERGER round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deplorable or to be lamented is unfortunate.

clue.text: Republican demand for money transactions

definitions.meaning: read as two words: an anti-monarchist calls for a prohibition on the monarch
the business of handling deposits and loans

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a call to outlaw the monarch it is a republican slogan; it also names the finance trade.

clue.text: Rock turn gets the bird for American star group

indicators.note: the short name for Gibraltar is turned to read the other way

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, often shortened to Gib
a dipper is a small diving water bird

explanation.surface: A wobble on a rock is followed by a bird appearing, in an American constellation tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is known as the Rock; 'turn' reverses GIB. In Britain this star group is called the Plough; a big dipper is also a British fairground rollercoaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans name the seven bright stars of Ursa Major by this term, the British Plough.

clue.text: Bump in boat

explanation.definitionFit: It means to shove clumsily into someone, and a flat-bottomed canal vessel.

clue.text: Clergyman working with prison

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A churchman does his job at a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral priest with a particular office holds this title.

clue.text: Church always offers comfort

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: The church always provides consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten or console someone is to comfort them.

clue.text: Money can make one thick-skinned

definitions.meaning: an old British slang word for cash
a large horned African or Asian beast with tough hide

explanation.surface: Being rich can make you insensitive.
explanation.definitionFit: It is dated British slang for cash, and the animal famous for its thick hide.

clue.text: Winning ball again and creating new platform, perhaps

definitions.meaning: in rugby, heeling is pushing the ball back out of a scrum with the feet, winning it, here done a second time
fitting a shoe with new raised backs, such as platforms

explanation.surface: A rugby side wins possession once more while building a new stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a rugby scrum players 'heel' the ball back to their own side.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting fresh heels on shoes, platform heels for instance, and heeling a ball out a second time share the word.

clue.text: Lamb, for example, in casseroles, say, is tasty

indicators.note: the letters run inside the words that follow, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: Lamb, say, cooked in a casserole, is delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia; 'Lamb' seems to be meat in the cooking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was a famous English writer of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Dread of strong punch

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
a right is a punch thrown with the right hand

explanation.surface: Someone is afraid of a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden terror or alarm is what dread amounts to here.
